purpose: Close the Branch fast-carrier force available for the Flintlock-equivalent operation and reorganize the historical four groups into three stronger groups after Branch legacy-carrier losses and GALVANIC repair casualties.
historical_baseline: Historical Flintlock used 6 CV + 6 CVL in four three-carrier TGs: Enterprise/Yorktown/Belleau Wood; Essex/Intrepid/Cabot; Bunker Hill/Monterey/Cowpens; Saratoga/Princeton/Langley, plus eight fast battleships.
branch_changes: Enterprise CV-6 and Saratoga CV-3 are permanent Branch losses and cannot be reinserted.
Wasp CV-7 survives the Branch and is an experienced fast carrier.
Lexington CV-16 is under major repair after GALVANIC and unavailable.
Independence CVL-22 is in long repair and unavailable.
Intrepid CV-11, Cabot CVL-28 and Langley CVL-27 are date-valid January additions.

GALVANIC teaches the US to avoid a weak isolated carrier group against surviving Japanese first-line carriers; the now-understrength historical TG58.4 is dissolved and its two CVLs are distributed to stronger groups.

task_groups.commander: Rear Adm. John W. Reeves Jr.
task_groups.role: Maloelap/Taroa suppression, northern/central CAP and flexible support
task_groups.derivation: Historical TG58.1 with Branch Wasp replacing lost Enterprise; Princeton redistributed from dissolved historical TG58.4.

cruiser_anchor: San Diego CL-53 class/AA-cruiser slot; exact named light-cruiser screen retained as historical fallback pending hull-level need
task_groups.derivation: Historical TG58.2 largely retained; Branch does not need to invent an extra deck.

task_groups.role: Kwajalein/Eniwetok suppression, reserve and western cover
task_groups.derivation: Historical TG58.3 reinforced by Langley and the heavy-cruiser pair from dissolved historical TG58.4.

screen_total_working.branch_cost_note: Franks is a permanent GALVANIC DD loss; US replacement depth can absorb one hull without reproducing the exact historical 35-DD list.

why_not_historical_31Jan: GALVANIC removes Lexington/Independence for the next operation, imposes repair/reorganization and logistics friction, and the US faces a healthier Marshall network plus three surviving Japanese first-line carriers. These factors justify a days-scale shift, not the superseded multi-week/month delay.
anti_overreach: Do not count Wasp as an Essex-class 90+ aircraft deck.
Do not reinsert Enterprise, Saratoga, Lexington CV-16 or Independence.
Do not treat 610 ready aircraft as 610 simultaneous strike aircraft; CAP/search/ASW/recovery reservations remain large.
D-Day is a working window until the clock reaches first strike/contact.
